messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Stan-mode indentation
parts:
I'm using stan-mode with emacs to edit stan source files, and I'm running into a major annoyance with indentation. When calling a user-defined function with a long function name and several arguments, I want to write

    my_long_user_defined_function(
      argument_expression_1, ..., argument_expression_n);

because I cannot fit the entire call on one line, but stan-mode keeps changing the indentation to

    my_long_user_defined_function(
                                  argument_expression_1, ..., argument_expression_n);

which completely defeats the purpose of putting the arguments on the following line, not to mention looking hideous.

Is there a way to turn off this behavior?

messages.author: 6ad178c9bfa534b7
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan-mode indentation
parts:
stan-mode is based off of emacs cc-mode, which has a very customizable indentation engine, which you can read about  here. It's based off of the syntatic class of the first element in the line, which in your example would be arglist-intro (you can find this using C-c C-s). You change the indentation rules using the variable c-offsets-alist. For your example, you'd want to add this to your init file. It will override the default indentation for lines beginning with arglist-intro.

(add-hook 'stan-mode-hook
 (setq c-offsets-alist
  '("stan" (arglist-intro . +))))

messages.author: 6ad178c9bfa534b7
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan-mode indentation
parts:
Add this to your init file to override it for all cc-mode languages

 '(c-offsets-alist (quote ((arglist-intro . +))))

Or you can create a new style / choose a style for c++-mode that you like better. cc-mode lets you customize everything, but frankly, I'm at a cargo cult level of understanding what it's doing. The section on Styles (http://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/ccmode/Styles.html#Styles) has a ton of info on it.
